title: Query Data (SELECT)
syntax:
SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name
FROM customer
ORDER BY customer_id
LIMIT 10;
note: Select only the columns you need; avoid SELECT * in production queries.

title: DDL Commands
note: DDL changes schema objects and may acquire locks; review its impact before running it in production.

title: DML Commands
note: Use a transaction and a precise WHERE clause for UPDATE or DELETE operations.

title: Filtering Data
syntax:
SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name, active
FROM customer
WHERE active = 1
  AND first_name ILIKE 'A%'
  AND customer_id BETWEEN 1 AND 100
ORDER BY last_name;
note: ILIKE performs case-insensitive matching in PostgreSQL; a leading wildcard can prevent efficient B-tree index use.

title: SQL Joins (Basics)
note: Put join predicates in ON; moving right-table filters into WHERE can unintentionally turn a LEFT JOIN into an INNER JOIN.

title: SQL Joins (Advanced)
note: Many-to-many joins can multiply rows; confirm the intended grain before aggregating results.

title: Set Operators
note: UNION removes duplicates, while UNION ALL preserves them and is usually faster.

title: SQL Functions
syntax:
SELECT customer_id,
       upper(first_name) AS first_name_upper,
       length(last_name) AS last_name_length,
       coalesce(email, 'unknown') AS email
FROM customer
LIMIT 10;
note: Functions operate per row unless they are aggregate or window functions.

title: String Functions
syntax:
SELECT customer_id,
       concat(first_name, ' ', last_name) AS full_name,
       upper(last_name) AS last_name_upper,
       left(email, 5) AS email_prefix,
       replace(email, '.org', '.example') AS masked_domain
FROM customer
LIMIT 10;
note: Use concat when nullable inputs are possible; it treats NULL arguments as empty strings.

title: Numeric Functions
syntax:
SELECT payment_id, amount,
       round(amount * 1.10, 2) AS amount_with_tax,
       abs(amount - 5.00) AS distance_from_five,
       ceil(amount) AS rounded_up
FROM payment
LIMIT 10;
note: Cast operands deliberately when integer division or precision could affect the result.

title: Date and Time Functions
syntax:
SELECT rental_id, rental_date, return_date,
       rental_date::date AS rental_day,
       date_trunc('month', rental_date) AS rental_month,
       return_date - rental_date AS rental_duration
FROM rental
WHERE rental_date >= date '2005-06-01'
LIMIT 10;
note: Timestamps in dvdrental are stored without time zone; apply time-zone conversion only when the data semantics require it.

title: NULL Functions
syntax:
SELECT rental_id,
       coalesce(return_date, now()) AS effective_return_date,
       nullif(staff_id, 0) AS nullable_staff_id
FROM rental
LIMIT 10;
note: NULL is not equal to anything, including NULL; use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL for null checks.

title: Case Statement
syntax:
SELECT payment_id, amount,
       CASE
           WHEN amount >= 8 THEN 'high'
           WHEN amount >= 4 THEN 'medium'
           ELSE 'low'
       END AS payment_band
FROM payment
LIMIT 10;
note: CASE returns the first matching branch, so order overlapping conditions from most specific to least specific.

title: Aggregate Functions
syntax:
SELECT customer_id,
       count(*) AS payment_count,
       sum(amount) AS total_paid,
       avg(amount) AS average_payment
FROM payment
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING sum(amount) >= 100
ORDER BY total_paid DESC;
note: WHERE filters rows before aggregation; HAVING filters aggregated groups.

title: Window Functions Basics
syntax:
SELECT customer_id, payment_id, amount,
       avg(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS customer_avg_payment
FROM payment
ORDER BY customer_id, payment_id;
note: Window functions retain the original row count, unlike GROUP BY aggregates.

title: Window Aggregate
syntax:
SELECT customer_id, payment_date, amount,
       sum(amount) OVER (
           PARTITION BY customer_id
           ORDER BY payment_date, payment_id
           ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
       ) AS running_total
FROM payment
ORDER BY customer_id, payment_date, payment_id;
note: Specify ROWS explicitly for running totals when ORDER BY values can tie.

title: Window Ranking
syntax:
SELECT customer_id, payment_id, amount,
       row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY amount DESC) AS row_num,
       rank() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY amount DESC) AS payment_rank,
       dense_rank() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY amount DESC) AS dense_payment_rank
FROM payment;
note: RANK leaves gaps after ties; DENSE_RANK does not. Add a stable tie-breaker for deterministic ROW_NUMBER results.

title: Window Value
syntax:
SELECT customer_id, payment_date, amount,
       lag(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY payment_date, payment_id) AS previous_amount,
       lead(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY payment_date, payment_id) AS next_amount,
       first_value(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY payment_date, payment_id) AS first_amount
FROM payment;
note: FIRST_VALUE uses the current window frame; define a frame explicitly when you need the partition-wide first value.

title: Subqueries
definition: To nest a query within another
syntax:
SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name
FROM customer
WHERE customer_id IN (
    SELECT customer_id
    FROM payment
    GROUP BY customer_id
    HAVING sum(amount) >= 100
);
note: Prefer EXISTS for existence checks, especially when the subquery may return many rows.

title: Common Table Expressions (CTE)
syntax:
WITH customer_spend AS (
    SELECT customer_id, sum(amount) AS total_paid
    FROM payment
    GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, cs.total_paid
FROM customer AS c
JOIN customer_spend AS cs ON cs.customer_id = c.customer_id
ORDER BY cs.total_paid DESC;
note: A CTE improves readability; PostgreSQL can inline non-recursive CTEs when it is safe to do so.

title: Views
note: A regular view stores its query, not its result; query performance still depends on the underlying tables and plan.

title: CTAS and Temp Tables
note: Temporary tables are session-scoped and are dropped automatically when the session ends.

title: Stored Procedures
note: Procedures are invoked with CALL; PostgreSQL functions are invoked inside expressions such as SELECT.

title: Triggers
note: Triggers execute implicitly and can make writes harder to reason about; keep their logic small and documented.

title: Indexes
note: Indexes speed qualifying reads but add storage and write overhead. Put commonly filtered leading columns first in a composite B-tree index.

title: Execution Plan
syntax:
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
SELECT c.customer_id, sum(p.amount) AS total_paid
FROM customer AS c
JOIN payment AS p ON p.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE p.payment_date >= timestamp '2005-06-01'
GROUP BY c.customer_id;
note: EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the query; use it carefully with expensive or mutating statements.

title: Partitions
definition: To split large tables by key
syntax:
CREATE TABLE payment_archive (
    payment_id integer NOT NULL,
    customer_id smallint NOT NULL,
    payment_date timestamp NOT NULL,
    amount numeric(5,2) NOT NULL
) PARTITION BY RANGE (payment_date);

CREATE TABLE payment_archive_2005_06
PARTITION OF payment_archive
FOR VALUES FROM ('2005-06-01') TO ('2005-07-01');

INSERT INTO payment_archive (payment_id, customer_id, payment_date, amount)
SELECT payment_id, customer_id, payment_date, amount
FROM payment
WHERE payment_date >= timestamp '2005-06-01'
  AND payment_date < timestamp '2005-07-01';
note: Partition pruning requires predicates that can be matched to the partition key. Partitioning is not a substitute for appropriate indexes.
